correctness.rationale: Writing A=2^a and B=2^b reduces the harmonious equation exactly to q(A+B-1)=(A-1)(2B-1). With D=A+B-1, gcd(D,A-1)=1, so D divides 2B-1; then D also divides 2A-1. The two size inequalities force A=B, after which q=A-1. The converse is direct. No finite search is used for the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete unbounded classification of a natural two-prime-support slice of harmonious pairs and explains the recurring examples (4,12), (8,56), (32,992), and beyond by a single Mersenne-prime mechanism. It is not an arbitrary finite cutoff: the family is defined intrinsically by prime support, and the result converts tabulated examples into an exact iff theorem.
